title: The hidden gift
hookLine: Zhuangzi's hunchback Shu is spared the army and fed by the state (Zhuangzi 4)
carry: a side the world's measuring stick misses

cards: The recruiters have come to town, rounding up men for the army, and every young man with a strong back has found somewhere to hide: the hayloft, an aunt's house, the reeds by the river. Except one.
He's strolling down the middle of the street, arms swinging, saying hello to the officers. Nobody stops him. Nobody looks twice.
His name, in the book of Zhuangzi, is Shu, and the reason nobody versions him is his body.

teach.h: A BODY THAT FITS NO MEASURE.
teach.b: First, who Shu is. Zhuangzi draws him in big, almost cartoon strokes: his chin tucked down by his navel, his shoulders higher than the top of his head, his hair knot pointing at the sky.
A body that fits none of the world's measures. Second, how he lives. He isn't helpless in the story.
He earns his food sewing and washing clothes, and by sifting grain he makes enough to feed others besides himself. Third, the turn.

teach.h: SPARED THE ARMY, FED BY THE STATE.
teach.b: When the army comes, he walks among the recruiters without fear. When the state calls up men for heavy labor, he's excused because of his condition.
When it hands out grain to the sick, he gets his share, and firewood too.

Then Zhuangzi draws the lesson, in paraphrase: if a man whose body is out of the usual shape can look after himself and live out his years, how much more someone whose virtue is out of the usual shape.
The chapter is set in a dangerous world, where being useful gets you used up.

This path met the useless tree in its first year; Shu is its neighbor in the same chapter, which ends, in paraphrase: everyone knows the use of the useful, but nobody knows the use of the useless. Fourth, what it isn't.
Zhuangzi doesn't say every limit is secretly a blessing, and nobody gets to tell you yours is.

teach.h: NOT A PROMISE. A TURNED PICTURE.
teach.b: He turns the picture once, to show a side the world's measuring stick misses.
The gift is hidden, partial, and still real.

how: Readers of the Zhuangzi, Daoists among them, read Shu and the useless tree together as stories about the use of the useless, and some return to them in times of illness, disability or failure.

o: a sage who hid in the reeds to escape the war
an army officer who drafted all the useful men
a man in Zhuangzi spared because he fit no measure

games.q: inside Shu's story — tap the pairs.
p: a body that fits none of the world's measures
he gets his share, and firewood
what nobody knows, the chapter ends

s: Zhuangzi says every limit is secretly a blessing
he turns the picture once to show what the world's measure misses; he promises nothing.
in the story, Shu earns his keep and feeds others
by sewing, washing clothes and sifting grain.
Shu hides when the army comes recruiting
he walks right among the recruiters without fear.

games.q: you're Shu. the recruiters have come to town, rounding up men for the army. what do you do?
o: hide in the hayloft with the others.
games.why: he walks among them freely. the body the world counts against him is the reason nobody versions him.

practice: Let one limit you live with come to mind, small enough to hold today: a knee that won't run, a shyness, no car, not enough money for what everyone else is doing.

Hold it without arguing, and ask it two quiet questions: what do you spare me from, and what do you leave room for? Maybe something comes, a slower walk where you notice more; maybe nothing does, and that's an honest answer too.

wordCard.voice: Shu, the man in Zhuangzi whose body didn't fit the world's measure, and who was spared and fed because of it. Today's word.

orig.note: classical Chinese, from the end of Zhuangzi chapter 4: the use of the useless (wú yòng zhī yòng).

carryVoice: Your line: a side the world's measuring stick misses. Zhuangzi turns the picture once, and lets you look. Day seven hundred twenty-nine, done.
